newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo trains to ban cellular phones.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo trains to ban cellular phones.

text.p: Passengers on most commuter trains in Tokyo will be banned from using cellular phones beginning next month, East Japan Railway Co (JR East) said on Saturday.
Officials of JR East, the biggest operators of commuter trains in the capital, said they would start a ban-the-phone campaign by posters and announcements in April.

The use of cellular phones on crowded Tokyo trains has recently become the target of public scorn, because people trying to speak into their phones shout above the noise of the train, making them obnoxious fellow-passengers.
The recent proliferation of portable telephones in Japan has triggered other problems.

The National Police Agency, releasing the first statistics of its kind last week, said that in the last six months of 1996 nine people died and 1,627 were injured in 1,140 traffic accidents while drivers were speaking on cellular phones,
The latest telephone company statistics show about one out of five Japanese owns a cellular phone. Altogether, there are about 25 million sets in operation.
